title: Introduction to a Poetics of Diversity
abstract: This book reproduces the texts of four lectures, followed by discussions, and two interviews with Lise Gauvin published in Introduction à une poétique du divers (1996); and also four further interviews from L’Imaginaire des langues (Lise Gauvin, 2010). It covers a wide range of topics but key recurring themes are creolization, language and langage , culture and identity, ‘monolingualism’, the ‘Chaos-world’ and the role of the writer. Migration and the various different kinds of migrants are also discussed, as is the difference between ‘atavistic’ and ‘composite’ communities, the art of translation, identity as a ‘rhizome’ rather than a single root, the Chaos-World and chaos theory, ‘trace thought’ as opposed to ‘systematic thought’, the relation between ‘place’ and the Whole-World, exoticism, utopias, a new definition of beauty as the realized quantity of differences, the status of literary genres and the possibility that literature as a whole will disappear. Four of the interviews (Chapters 6, 7, 8 and 9) relate to particular works that Glissant has published: Tout-monde, Le monde incrée, La Cohée du Lamentin, Une nouvelle région du monde . Many of these themes have been explored in his previous works, but here, because in all the chapters we see Glissant interacting with the questions and views of other people, they are presented in a particularly accessible form.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Introduction to a Poetics of Diversity (2020), published by Liverpool University Press, has been cited 54 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 10% of works in its field and year.

Full narrative

Introduction to a Poetics of Diversity by Édouard Glissant was published by Liverpool University Press in 2020. Conceptually, the work connects to Poetics, Creolization, Identity (music), Literature and TRACE (psycholinguistics).

OpenAlex records 54 citations. That places it in the top 10% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2024 with 28 citing works. Notable citing venues include Dancecult, Time & Society and Journal of Postcolonial Writing. The citing works include 23 book chapters, 16 journal articles and 6 books. They come from 10 countries, led by Germany, the United States and the United Kingdom.

Open Library reports a combined count of 2 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Reduced inequalities among the Sustainable Development Goals.
